Source: A 56-year-old man presents from prison with 1 month of subjective fevers, chills, cough, and night sweats.
He has never smoked cigarettes but does have a history of opiate use prior to incarceration.
His temperature is 100.8°F (38.2°C), blood pressure is 142/88 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and respirations are 12/min.
Physical exam reveals a thin, ill-appearing man.
He noticed a gradual weight loss over the past year despite no changes to his diet or physical activity.
Pulmonary auscultation reveals faint, inspiratory crackles in the right upper lobe.
He does not take any medications.
